findings.reason: without a control that mutates the code path the test pins (change the emitted field and require the test to redden), a node can satisfy every stated measure while deleting the property the test exists to protect, and the plan's only guard against that is the node's own reading of a commit.
findings.text: the twelve new sections share one negative control, "reverting each repair makes its id fail again", yet their dominant repair is re-freezing a byte-pinned or closed-set expectation to "the intended new value"; restoring the old expectation makes the id fail by construction, so the control passes for any edit that reaches green, including one that re-freezes the snapshot to whatever the changed code now emits and thereby pins an unintended regression

findings.reason: each of those sections' Deliverable says a node that finds one unintended change "changes neither that code nor that test, and reports the run blocked", so in a mixed-cause node every intended repair it had already made is discarded with the blocked verdict and the next section must redo them; one cause per node lets each verdict close on its own evidence.
findings.text: §46 bundles discards, queue placement, congestion routing, hold counts and recovery holds ("Discards, queue placement, congestion routing, hold counts and recovery holds read states the admission pass no longer produces"), §47 bundles follower transitions, sweep recording and producer retry/bound behaviour, and §49 bundles edit-plan refusal shape, response-budget truncation, roadmap gate edges, ledger view lists and fingerprint op refusal

findings.reason: a reader or coordinator that trusts the header reads this plan as 98% complete and deprioritises the twelve remaining cause groups, and the doccheck warning is the instrument the repo uses to detect exactly this drift.FINDING reasoning docs/plans/the-suite-is-green-at-head.html:841 — §52's Why claims "These 5 ids fail in any worktree, the census tree and a worktree whose path contains `reckon` alike", but rerunning its five ids at this node's base (`12b7fea24`, a provisioned worktree whose path contains `reckon`) leaves 4 passing and only `tests/test_a_worker_cannot_walk_the_crew_home.py::test_the_sync_installer_binds_the_walk_guard_behind_the_git_guard_flag` failing (2 failed, 86 passed; repro-s51-s52.log); the census's other four failures are scaffolding — `test_hook_installer.py:220` fails `assert INTERPRETER.is_file()` because the unprovisioned extraction resolved it to `/tmp/mcintos-1291586-suite-ffcM/.venv/bin/python` — WOULD_CHANGE_THE_PLAN: yes — REASON: as written the section sends a node to look for a mount-resolution defect in four tests that pass unchanged, and its done-when ("the listed ids pass at the head") is satisfied for them before any work, so the section both misdirects the repair and loses the ability to show that any repair it did make is load-bearing.
findings.text: the header carries `<meta name="plan-impl" content="0.98">` while the plan's own declarations derive 0.599359, and `reckon.doccheck` reports it: "plan-impl meta is 0.98 but the section records derive 0.599359 (impl_source: declarations); the file and the server disagree until the next write lands" — thirteen sections (s3 and s41–s52) are `implementable` and open

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — §52 cites `pathcheck-main.log` for "These 5 ids … pass in the main checkout", but that log records six tests, two of them failing, and those two are §48's and §51's ids, so at most four of §52's five ids are shown there.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — the shared template's negative control ("reverting each repair makes its id fail again") cannot falsify a wrong re-freeze of a byte-pinned test, which is the stated repair for most of these ids.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — every gate log is required "under the run directory" and every cited measurement sits on a durable path (`~/.cache/reckon-suite-census/c8a082c99e3023b61c438143e898bd0039315149-rerun/rerun.log`, `…/pathcheck-main.log`), all of which resolve on this host.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new sections introduce no symbols or comments; the only identifiers are test node ids and existing module paths, and no unit id, ticket number or version tag reaches code.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §52 states a root cause ("the installer and guard resolve the repository through the workstation's mounts, which name the main checkout") that its own ids do not support at the node's base: four of the five pass unchanged in a provisioned worktree here; the plan header also states `plan-impl` 0.98 while its own declarations derive 0.599359.
rubric_items.single_goal: a finding — §46, §47 and §49 each name several distinct mechanisms in one node, and one unintended change in any of them blocks the whole run's other repairs.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — each of the twelve new sections s41–s52 carries an open followup (f-tsigah-041 … f-tsigah-052) whose prompt names its own section, `plan-section-depends-on` still declares only `s32`, and the twelve write-path sets are pairwise disjoint, so no node waits on a relationship the plan omits.
